project.objective: Did Gertrudis Hoffmans and her husband Petrus Jansen of Wanroij, North Brabant, Netherlands have a daughter named Elisabeth, baptized 1713, in addition to their three known sons (christened 1709-1717)?

questions.question: Does a baptismal record exist for a daughter named Elisabeth born to Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans of Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, Netherlands, circa 1713?
questions.rationale: The research objective asks whether a daughter named Elisabeth was baptized in 1713 alongside three known sons (baptized 1709–1717). The Wanroij Dutch Reformed and Catholic parish registers for Noord-Brabant circa 1700–1720 are the primary record class for this question; FamilySearch holds digitized Noord-Brabant DTB registers and the WieWasWie index covers many of them. This single question maps directly to the objective and is testable: a positive baptism entry confirms the daughter; an exhaustive negative search of all surviving registers for the period constitutes negative evidence that she did not exist or was not recorded.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two representations of the Wanroij DTB register entry for 30 March 1713 were consulted: (1) the derivative archival index via FamilySearch collection 2704829 (BHIC/OpenArch, src_001, ark:/61903/1:1:QL69-GBJC), and (2) the original DTB register page image (src_002, image 005844878_00049, transcribed in full). Both confirm: Elisabet baptized 30 March 1713, Wanroij, Noord-Brabant; father Petri Jansen; mother Gertrudis Geerts (= Gertrudis Hoffmans = KN19-Q19 — patronymic form used interchangeably with family surname in the same register; confirmed by adjacent Gerardus entry on image 48). Adjacent sibling entries in the same register confirm the correct family. The collection-ID transposition (2704729 vs. 2704829) was identified and corrected. The original image was located by volumetric estimation across 84-image volume 005844878. External sites (WieWasWie/BHIC) were deferred in autonomous mode but collection 2704829 aggregates the same BHIC index data; the positive finding was obtained there. Limitation: src_001 and src_002 are representations of the same DTB entry and share the same informant (parish priest); they count as one evidence unit. For pre-1811 Dutch Catholic baptisms, the DTB register is the primary and typically sole record type, so this structural limitation cannot be overcome by further searching.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes. Original DTB register image (src_002, image 005844878_00049) and derivative index (src_001) both confirm Elisabeth baptized 30 March 1713 in Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, daughter of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans/Geerts. Question answered affirmatively with primary direct evidence.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch collections 1778468 (Netherlands Births and Baptisms 1564-1910) and 2704829 (Netherlands Archival Indexes Vital Records 1600-2000, aggregating BHIC data) searched; original DTB register browse-volume 005844878 browsed across images 27, 35, 48, 49; marriage record confirmed in tree (7YSN-34G, 5 Feb 1709). Name variants tried: Jansen/Janssen, Hoffmans/Hofmans, Gerits/Geerts. For 1713 Noord-Brabant no other accessible repository holds this record type.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Derivative index (src_001, collection 2704829, BHIC/OpenArch) followed to original DTB register image (src_002, image 005844878_00049) and transcribed in full. Original successfully accessed.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Structural limitation: src_001 and src_002 both represent the same underlying DTB register entry (same informant, same event); they count as one evidence unit. No genuinely independent record type exists for a 1713 Dutch Catholic baptism in pre-civil-registration Netherlands (civil registration 1811+; burial and marriage DTBs share the same provenance family). One original primary-source evidence unit accessed at the highest quality tier.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: src_002 is an original source (actual parish register image, volume 005844878_00049), primary information (recorded at baptism by parish priest), direct evidence (names child, date 30 March 1713, parents Petri Jansen and Gertrudis Geerts, godparents Martinus Geerts and Anna Jan Nelissen). Highest GPS classification achieved.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Apparent surname discrepancy resolved: mother recorded as 'Geertrudis Gerits' (src_001 index), 'Gertrudis Geerts' (src_002 original image 49), and 'Gertrudis Hoffmans' (same register image 48, Gerardus baptism 6 Aug 1711). All are patronymic vs. family-surname variants for the same individual — the register itself alternates forms across adjacent entries. LZ6D-XC4 (Gerrit Gerrits Hoffmans, father of KN19-Q19) in the tree makes the derivation explicit. No genuine conflicts.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The original parish register entry has been located and transcribed; it matches the derivative index. No unsearched record type in 18th-century Dutch Catholic tradition would independently record this specific baptism. The naming discrepancy is internally resolved by the source. A future researcher might find Elisabeth in later records (a marriage or death entry in a subsequent DTB register), which would further corroborate her existence but could not plausibly deny the documented 1713 baptism.

items.rationale: WieWasWie (wiewaswie.nl) is the national Dutch genealogy index aggregating DTB registers including Noord-Brabant, with index & images, free. BHIC (bhic.nl — Brabants Historisch Informatie Centrum) is the provincial archive for Noord-Brabant and likely holds the most complete searchable index for Wanroij registers. Searching both indexed portals before browsing images is the fastest and most efficient route. Search for baptisms of children of Petrus Jansen (variants: Janssen, Jansz) and Gertrudis Hoffmans (variants: Hofmans, Hoffmann) in Wanroij, ca. 1700–1720, specifically looking for a daughter named Elisabeth ca. 1713. Also note any other children to confirm we have the right family.

FamilySearch collection 1778468 (Netherlands, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1910) contains 1,572,754 indexed records and is the primary indexed baptism collection on FamilySearch for the Netherlands. Search for Elisabeth Jansen / Janssen baptized in Wanroij or Noord-Brabant ca. 1710–1716. Also search for children of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans to confirm family. Note: this is a legacy collection with no further additions, so a negative result here does not preclude records being found in the browse-only volumes. Try surname variants: Jansen / Janssen / Jansz; Hoffmans / Hofmans / Hoffmann.

FamilySearch collection 2704729 (Netherlands, Archival Indexes, Vital Records, 1600-2000) contains 46.5 million records with images and aggregates many Noord-Brabant archival indexes. This broader index may capture Wanroij baptisms not covered by collection 1778468. Search for Petrus Jansen / Gertrudis Hoffmans children baptized in Wanroij or Noord-Brabant ca. 1700–1720.

FamilySearch image volume 005844878_001_M96P-YNM (84 images) covers Wanroij baptisms, deaths, and marriages 1656–1723 — the most targeted volume for the ca. 1713 research window. It is 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable: must be browsed image-by-image. Browse for all baptismal entries ca. 1709–1717 to locate the known sons (confirming we have the right family) and identify whether Elisabeth appears ca. 1713. Catholic records in this region are in Latin. Access via FamilySearch collection 2037960 (Netherlands, Noord-Brabant, Church Records) → Religion/Other → Wanroij → Baptisms/Volume. Alternatively use Genealogie Werkbalk (genealogiewerkbalk.nl/fs/).

FamilySearch image volumes 005864409_002_M99N-2VV (1,059 images) and 005864410 (3,099 images) cover Wanroij baptisms 1655–1811. These larger volumes provide supplemental coverage and may contain entries not present in volume 005844878_001 (e.g., if the records are from different series or registers). Browse for Elisabeth Jansen ca. 1713 if not found in volume 005844878_001, and to confirm or extend the sibling list. All are 0% indexed — browse-only.

A search of the Wanroij DTB marriage register for the marriage of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans serves two purposes: (1) it confirms the couple as a documented unit with a known marriage date, providing a chronological anchor for when children could have been born; (2) it may supply additional identifying details (ages, parents' names, witnesses) that help distinguish this couple from any namesakes. Volume 005844878_001_M96P-YNM (84 images, 1656–1723) covers marriages (*Trouwen*) in addition to baptisms and deaths for this period. Volume 005864411 (3,080 images, 1655–1811) also covers Wanroij marriages. Browse both for the Jansen–Hoffmans marriage entry.

hypotheses.claim: The woman recorded as 'Geertrudis Gerits' (src_001 derivative index) and 'Gertrudis Geerts' (src_002 original DTB register image 49) in the 30 March 1713 baptism of Elisabet at Wanroij is the same individual as Gertrudis Hoffmans (KN19-Q19) in the project tree.
hypotheses.notes: Patronymic forms 'Gerits/Geerts' (daughter of Gerrit) derive from the given name of Gertrudis's father Gerrit Gerrits Hoffmans (LZ6D-XC4), documented in the tree as KN19-Q19's father via R3 (ParentChild). The same DTB register uses 'Gertrudis Hoffmans' on image 48 (Gerardus baptism, 6 Aug 1711, godfather Anthonius Hoffmans) and 'Gertrudis Geerts' on image 49 (Elisabet baptism, 30 Mar 1713) — alternating family surname and patronymic for the same woman in consecutive family entries, by the same priest. Same spouse Petrus Jansen appears in both entries. This is a documented naming convention in early-18th-century Noord-Brabant Catholic registers. Identity resolution supported: cross-register internal corroboration by the same source resolves the apparent discrepancy.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: FamilySearch collection 1778468 (Netherlands Births and Baptisms, 1564–1910) and collection 2704829 (Netherlands Archival Indexes Vital Records, 1600–2000, aggregating BHIC/OpenArch data) were searched with name variants Jansen/Janssen and Hoffmans/Hofmans/Gerits/Geerts. Collection 1778468 returned no entries for the target family; collection 2704829 returned the indexed Elisabeth Jansen baptism record (ark:/61903/1:1:QL69-GBJC). The original DTB register volume 005844878 (84 images, Wanroij 1656–1723) was browsed across images 27, 35, 48, and 49; the target entry was located on image 49. External sites WieWasWie and BHIC were deferred in autonomous mode, but collection 2704829 aggregates the same BHIC index data and yielded the positive finding. Marriage of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans already confirmed in tree (source 7YSN-34G, dated 5 Feb 1709). A future search for Elisabeth in later Wanroij DTB volumes (a marriage record or burial) or in baptism records of any children she may have had would provide a genuinely independent corroboration and could advance the tier to proved.

## Baptism of Elisabeth Jansen, Wanroij, 30 March 1713: Daughter of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans

**Research question:** Did Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans of Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, Netherlands, have a daughter named Elisabeth baptized circa 1713, in addition to their three known sons (Joannes, baptized 1709; Gerardus, baptized 1711; Joannes, baptized 1717)?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of evidence strongly suggests that Elisabeth Jansen, baptized 30 March 1713 at Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, was a daughter of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans.

### Primary Evidence: Original DTB Register

The original Catholic DTB (Dopen/Trouwen/Begraven) parish register for Wanroij, spanning 1656–1723, contains the following entry transcribed from the Latin on folio image 005844878_00049:

> *30 martij baptizata e Elisabet, filia Petri Jansen, et Gertrudis Geerts; ss Martinus Geerts, et Anna Jan Nelißen.*

"30 March [1713], baptized was Elisabeth, daughter of Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Geerts; godparents: Martinus Geerts and Anna Jan Nelißen."

This is an original source — the actual parish register page — with primary information recorded at the time of baptism by the parish priest acting in an official capacity, and constitutes direct evidence bearing on the research question.[^1]

### Corroborating Derivative Index

A derivative archival index compiled by the Brabants Historisch Informatie Centrum (BHIC) via OpenArch and indexed on FamilySearch records the same event: Elisabeth Jansen, baptized 30 March 1713, Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, father Petrus Jansen, mother Geertrudis Gerits.[^2] As a derivative of the same DTB register entry and sharing the same informant (the parish priest), this index and the original constitute one evidence unit, not two independent sources.

### Mother's Naming Discrepancy Resolved

The mother's surname appears in three variant forms across sources: "Gertrudis Hoffmans" (as recorded in the same DTB register for the baptism of Gerardus, 6 August 1711, image 005844878_00048, with godfather Anthonius Hoffmans), "Gertrudis Geerts" (the Elisabeth entry, image 005844878_00049), and "Geertrudis Gerits" (the derivative index). These are not different individuals; they are naming-convention variants for the same person.

In early-eighteenth-century Catholic DTB registers for Noord-Brabant, women were commonly recorded by their patronymic (derived from the father's given name) in some entries and by their hereditary family surname in others. The patronymics "Geerts" and "Gerits" both derive from the given name "Gerrit." Gerrit Gerrits Hoffmans (tree person LZ6D-XC4), whose primary given name is Gerrit, is documented as Gertrudis Hoffmans's father via a ParentChild relationship in the project tree. His given name directly generates the patronymic "Geerts/Gerits" for a daughter. The alternation of "Hoffmans" and "Geerts" in adjacent entries of the same DTB register — recorded by the same priest for children of the same couple — confirms this is a naming-convention variation, not evidence of a different person. The corroborating Gerardus entry on image 005844878_00048 further confirms the family surname through godfather Anthonius Hoffmans.

### Evidence Assessment

**Strengths:** The primary evidence is an original Catholic parish register, read directly from the digitized image and transcribed in full. The information is primary (recorded at time of baptism by the officiating priest in an official capacity), and the evidence is direct (names the child, parents, date, and place explicitly). All assertions are classified at the highest GPS tier — original source, primary information, direct evidence.

**Limitation — single evidence unit:** The derivative index (src_001) and the original register image (src_002) both represent the same DTB entry recorded by the same parish priest. Per GPS independence principles, sources with the same informant count as one evidence unit. In pre-civil-registration Netherlands (civil registration began 1811), the DTB register is the primary and typically sole record type for Catholic baptismal events; no genuinely independent corroborating record type existed for a 1713 baptism. This structural limitation — inherent to the question type and period, not a research gap — prevents a "proved" conclusion under strict GPS Component 1 requirements.

A future search for Elisabeth Jansen in later Wanroij DTB records (a marriage entry or burial record), or in baptism records for any children she may have had, would provide a genuinely independent corroboration from a different event and informant, and could advance this conclusion to "proved" if found.

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly suggests that Petrus Jansen and Gertrudis Hoffmans of Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, had a daughter named Elisabeth, baptized in the Catholic parish of Wanroij on 30 March 1713. The original DTB register entry (image 005844878_00049), transcribed from the Latin and confirmed against the derivative index, is the authoritative primary record for this event. The apparent surname variation for the mother is fully explained and internally corroborated by the same register. The conclusion is rated **probable** due to the structural single-evidence-unit limitation inherent to this record type and era — not from any weakness in the quality or directness of the available evidence.

[^1]: Wanroij Catholic DTB Register, 1656–1723, baptisms; entry for Elisabet [Jansen], 30 March 1713; FamilySearch image group 005844878, image 00049; image 005844878_00049.jpg; original parish register, Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, Netherlands; accessed 2026-08-03.

[^2]: "Nederland, Indexen van de Archieven, Primaire Archiefstukken (BS en DTB), 1600-2000", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QL69-GBJC : accessed 3 August 2026), Entry for Elisabeth Jansen and Petrus Jansen, 30 Mar 1713.

# Locality Guide: Wanroij, Noord-Brabant, Netherlands (ca. 1700–1720)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Pre-1815 name:** Wanroij, Brabant, Netherlands (Generaliteitsland under the Dutch Republic)
- **Post-1815 name:** Wanroij, North Brabant, Netherlands (municipality, formed 1815; merged 1993)
- **Religious denomination:** Predominantly Roman Catholic — records in Latin
- **Key context:** Wanroij was in the Generaliteitsland, governed directly by the States-General. Civil registration did not exist; all vital records were kept by the Catholic parish (DTB registers).

## Boundary changes
- Pre-1815: Wanroij, Brabant, Netherlands
- From 1815: Wanroij, North Brabant, Netherlands
- The same physical DTB registers span both periods — treat as one continuous record set.

## Church records (DTB) — primary source for this period
- **Language:** Latin (Catholic)
- **Record types:** Baptisms (Dopen), Marriages (Trouwen), Burials (Begraven)
- **Coverage:** Baptisms from 1655; burials and marriages from 1655–1663 onward

## Research tips
1. Search WieWasWie and BHIC before browsing FS images.
2. Volume 005844878_001 (84 images, 1656–1723) is highest priority.
3. Catholic records in Latin — use Dutch and Latin word lists.
4. Surname variants: Jansen/Janssen/Jansz; Hoffmans/Hofmans/Hoffman.
5. Search neighboring parishes (Westerbeek, Mill, Sint Anthonis) if not found in Wanroij.
6. FS collection 2037960 browse path: Religion → Municipality (Wanroij) → Record Type/Volume.
7. Genealogie Werkbalk (genealogiewerkbalk.nl/fs/) offers an alternative browse interface.
